thread:
Evan: open question from the rollout workshop: should our fallback system use a single org-wide stable anchor, or a per-tenant anchor (or something in between)? we're seeing cross-tenant noise when we mix traffic and then fallback toggles rapidly
Lucy: my vote is a 'soft-anchor' approach. keep a per-tenant anchor if we have a confidence score for that tenant; otherwise fall back to a global anchor. soft-anchor means traffic routing prefers tenant anchor but will accept global if confidence low.
Priya: +1 to soft-anchor. define confidence by recent sample volume + stability (low variance). proposal: require min_samples >= 300 AND variance_ratio < 1.5 to use tenant anchor; else use global.
Marta: also add anchor decay: confidence decays over time (half-life 48h). that avoids stale anchors for low-traffic tenants. store last_seen_ts so we can compute decay quickly.
Ben: operational cost: per-tenant anchors mean KV reads at routing time. mitigate by caching anchors in the routing proxy with short TTL (30s) and by sharding anchor tables. we'll need a fast path that avoids a KV call on the hot path for most requests.
Evan: good call. how do we avoid thrash when many tenants have tiny samples (create many tiny anchors)?
Priya: limit active per-tenant anchors to tenants with traffic > X qps or samples > Y in last 24h. otherwise group into a pooled anchor bucket ("low-traffic bucket") that uses global anchor.
Lucy: telemetry: do a combined signal not just p95. weight signals like latency_delta, spike_count (sudden error bursts), and semantic-quality-check (a small eval set). different from earlier: use sample-adjusted scoring so small samples are penalized.
Marta: math suggestion: compute posterior P(canary_worse_by_delta | data) using a bayesian model on rate and latency. require posterior >= 0.975 AND adjusted_score >= 0.75 to trigger auto-fallback. adjusted_score = raw_score * (1 - exp(-samples/scale)). set scale=400 so small samples reduce the score heavily.
observability-bot: ALERT: canary/model-v3 p95 up 28% in eu-central; samples=160; error-burst=0.8%. link: https://obs.local/d/xxxx/canary-v3
Ben: samples < 300 so don't auto-fallback. instead create a high-priority Ops card and increase sample ingestion (probe more hosts).
Evan: fallback choreography: prefer staged rampdown over abrupt cut unless both error-rate > 2% AND p95 > 500ms. default ramp: reduce canary by 20% every 60s until anchor at 90% or canary drained. for severe thresholds, immediate circuit (kill).
Priya: logging: every fallback must emit structured metadata: reason_code, posterior, adjusted_score, sample_count, anchor_used, fallback_action. surface that in Console and in Optimize's regression UI.
Lucy: implementation sketch for anchor table:
```
# key: (tenant_id, model_family)
anchor_version, confidence_score, last_seen_ts, sample_count, warmed_cache_bool
ttl: 14d, eviction: low-traffic->global
shard by tenant_id % 128
```
Ben: proxy-side cache: LRU with 30s TTL, background refresher that warms cache for tenants with rising traffic. that avoids KV on every request.
Marta: test plan: build a canary-sim harness that can inject realistic jitter, correlated spikes, and semantic regressions. run sim for a week of traffic patterns and tune scale & thresholds. also run chaos experiments where global anchor is unhealthy to ensure graceful degradation.
Evan: responsibilities: @Priya tune the Bayesian priors + score weights; @Marta write an RFC with anchor lifecycle, decay math, fallback state machine, and API for ops to override; @Ben prototype proxy cache + shard layout; @Lucy own telemetry schema and Console integration.
Priya: i'll start with priors that favor anchor stability (conservative): prior odds = 3:1 in favor of anchor. will iterate after sims.
Ben: one more ops note: record all auto-fallbacks and expose an audit endpoint so SRE can replay the decision with the same inputs. helps postmortems.
Evan: action item for Ops: temporarily disable auto-fallback until sims complete and until min_samples rule (300) is enforced. will reconvene after RFC review. thanks all.
